question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}x, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 1\le x<2\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0 \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
